request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name]

Sex: Male

Age: 76 years

Medical Record No.: [Number]

Hospital Admission Date: [Date]

Discharge Date: [Date]

Hospital Course:

A 76-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with an incidental 4 cm left renal mass, which was treated with a left partial nephrectomy. Upon pathological examination, it was discovered that the patient was suffering from WHO/ISUP grade 1, TNM stage pT1 clear cell RCC, with the resection margin positive for the tumor.

The patient underwent a right radical orchiectomy when he was found to have a metastatic tumor in the right testis. The metastatic tumor was two centimeters in size, and it was confined to the testicular parenchyma.

Fourteen months after the orchiectomy, he underwent a completion left radical nephrectomy due to the recurrence of the tumor.

Ongoing imaging surveillance discovered several soft tissue masses in the left posterior chest wall, as well as masses in the pancreas. A two-centimeter enhancing mass was found in the upper pole of the right kidney 87 months following the orchiectomy.

The patient has been offered systemic therapy of VEGF inhibitor and discharged with continued medical supervision. He is alive with disease, 93 months post-orchiectomy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Status:

The patient is discharged with continued medical supervision.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The chapter letter is **C**, because the condition is a malignant neoplasm. The two digits are **64**, the category for malignant neoplasm of the kidney, except renal pelvis.

The patient was admitted for an incidental 4 cm left renal mass. He had a left partial nephrectomy, and pathology confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma (pT1, WHO/ISUP grade 1). That kidney malignancy is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode.

The summary also describes later events over many months. These include the testicular metastasis, the completion nephrectomy for recurrence, the chest wall, pancreatic and right kidney lesions, and the offer of VEGF-inhibitor therapy. All of these follow from the same primary renal cell carcinoma, so they do not change the principal diagnosis. The procedures performed are not the diagnosis either.

CODE: C64
